reviews.text:
Dear Natarsha Rathmell

Thank you very much for visiting us.
We also appreciate your high rating.
We sincerely look forward to seeing you again.
A cosy quiet cafe and had some fun time with exotic animals, recommend. You could even touch the owls!

I visited this establishment a few days ago and left disappointed and concerned about the living conditions of several animals. Numerous reviews have reported the same problems for months, with no visible changes. I would therefore like to suggest a few suggestions for improvement to try and help you make progress…

The hedgehogs: their enclosures contained mainly sand and a small hiding place. They need a deeper substrate for digging, more tunnels, and more hiding places. A rotation system would also allow hedgehogs not on public display to rest in suitable areas. We were alone in the café, and at least eight hedgehogs were accessible! Finally, all visitors could feed them, and some seemed particularly overweight: individual monitoring of their weight and diet would be important.

The meerkat: it was tied to a leash less than a meter long and constantly tried to scratch the ground without being able to dig… It needs a larger space, with a deeper substrate, burrows, climbing structures, and opportunities for foraging. Its tethering and living conditions should be reassessed.

The owls: one seemed to be trying to fly, but its approximately 40 cm tether prevented it. Both remained on artificial grass perches, with no apparent possibility of moving freely. Why not offer them a suitable aviary, with natural perches, enrichment activities, and quiet retreat areas? Rotating them would also allow them to rest out of sight of visitors, given that there are two of them.

I am not an expert, but these observations concern me. Animal welfare should not be limited to providing food and shelter: animals must be able to move, explore, hide, and express their natural behaviors. What I am suggesting here seems to me the bare minimum for their well-being.

Well-treated animals also contribute to a more positive experience for visitors and encourage them to return. Improving their living conditions would therefore be beneficial for them as well as for the facility.

I would like to add that the staff was kind and welcoming. The hamsters and guinea pigs, on the other hand, seemed to be in rather satisfactory conditions.

I sincerely hope that these remarks will be heard and followed by concrete improvements.
Friendly staff . Our kids love holding the hedgehogs
I was very happy that I could touch not only hedgehogs, but also owls and meerkats. You can also buy treats for them.
This was a terrible experience. Incredibly sad to see the animals in a dirty encircoent being harassed by many people and clearly distressed and trying to hide. Do not recommend.

TL;DR: Friendly staff and cute hedgehogs, but left with mixed feelings. The hedgehogs and guinea pigs in particular appeared stressed, and their small living spaces raised concerns for me about their quality of life.

Long version:
I have mixed feelings about this place. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the hedgehogs and other animals are obviously very cute. However their living spaces appeared to be very small cages or basins.

Most of the hedgehogs seemed quite stressed during our visit. When a gloved hand came close to them, they would flinch, tense up their spikes and appear to breathe rapidly. When they weren’t being fed or interacted with, they often seemed to try to hide from view. I obviously can’t know exactly what they were experiencing, but seeing these behaviours repeatedly made me uncomfortable and concerned about how much space they have to retreat from interaction.

The guinea pigs seemed to show some similar behaviour, although the meerkat and hamsters didn’t seem particularly bothered by the interactions.

We arrived in the afternoon so they must have had lots of interaction already. We mostly just let them be after noticing their discomfort.

What stood out was the contrast with a cat cafe we visited just a few days earlier. There the cats generally seemed more relaxed and there were clear rules to prohibit guests from disturbing them when asleep. Perhaps a similar rule could be helpful for the animals, but I understand it’d be difficult given the purpose of the store.
We went on a Monday afternoon and managed to walk in with 4 adults and 2 kids. Great time here, staff are so friendly and helpful.
Small cozy place like a mini petting zoo where u can visit the little animals and take some cute photos.
We had an amazing time! Some of the animals were busy sleeping, but the ones we interacted with (especially Hanpen the Meerkat) were so lovable and sweet.
Amazing experience and a great deal!
So fun and cute to play with the animals!

I was already really enjoying exploring the area but the sheer JOY when I saw these hedgehogs, I cannot describe.

The drinks are from a vending machine but I really enjoyed my ice coffee. The hedgehogs were unexpectedly active (we were there about 3pm). The meerkat seemed a little distressed and the owls were pretty chill
Just magical. Hedgehogs were the best, but the baby meerkat (Samira?) made my day! Staff were lovely as well, and they know the animals and care for them, which is really nice.
Very Cute Animals, Calm And Relaxed And Very Interested In Humans. Cozy Vibe, Loads Of Animals, Including Owls, Meerkats, Hamsters, Guinea Pigs, And Hedgehogs.
Its just sad... every animal there looked frustrated and sad. It is basically prison for hedgehogs. If you love animals, dont  go there, you dont want to see it, believe me

I was glad that the animal smells weren't too strong. You get one drink every 30 minutes from a self-service vending machine. There were two very small owls. They were quiet and cute. The meerkats were very friendly. The hedgehogs were only interested in treats and were rather cold, but overall the animals were calm. With owls, guinea pigs, meerkats, hedgehogs, and hamsters, one hour just isn't enough time. You can't interact with the hamsters if they're still small, so it's lucky if you happen to see one come out of its cage. When I went, only the golden hamsters were available for interaction. I understand that you're responsible for any droppings, but I wish they would provide a trash can for disposing of used tissues.
